title: South Korean Finance Minister Sees Chip Boom Lasting Through 2027; Maeil Warns of 2029 Memory "Red Ocean"
body: South Korea's Minister of Economy and Finance Lee Hyoung-il said on October 17, on the sidelines of the IMF–World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok, that the semiconductor boom would last "at least until next year," citing a still-wide gap between supply and demand as supply continues to expand.

SK hynix's second-quarter operating profit surged 557% year on year, and management reiterated that demand will outstrip supply through 2030; CEO Kwak Noh-jung said in August that the memory shortage would persist into 2030. Over the past year, Samsung Electronics shares rose roughly 150% and SK hynix about 250%.

Volatility remains sharp: on October 13 Samsung fell 7.5% intraday to 231,750 won and SK hynix dropped 8.4% as the KOSPI lost nearly 7% to 5,944.31 points, and on October 15 the index plunged 7.57% in a single session. Elon Musk responded on X that China "will produce a lot of RAM in 2028."

South Korea's Maeil Business Newspaper argued in an October 15 column that the period through 2028 is a "safe zone," but warned that new capacity flooding the market from 2029 onward means a memory "red ocean in 2029" and a downturn in 2030. SK hynix reports third-quarter results on October 28 and Samsung on October 29; US September CPI rose 3.7% year on year.

title: Report: Samsung to Use TSMC 3nm for NVIDIA's Custom NVHBM Base Die
body: South Korea's Seoul Economic Daily reported on October 18 that Samsung Electronics will outsource the base die at the bottom of NVIDIA's custom HBM, "NVHBM," to TSMC on its 3nm process. NVIDIA unveiled NVHBM on August 26, 2026; its key design move is relocating the GPU's (which NVIDIA calls XPU) memory controller into the HBM stack's base die alongside an in-house PHY.

Per the report, NVIDIA requires all three suppliers — Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron — to build the base die on TSMC 3nm while the core die uses sixth-generation 1c DRAM. UBS estimates 2027 HBM demand will grow 91% year-on-year to about 615 billion Gb against only around 546 billion Gb of new supply, leaving a roughly 10% shortfall. Samsung is separately validating base-die production on its own 2nm process.

Caveat: as of publication, NVIDIA, Samsung, TSMC, SK Hynix and Micron had issued no official statements; all details trace to the newspaper's anonymous industry sources. SK Hynix previously held the lead NVIDIA HBM supplier position on the strength of its early base-die work.

title: Zhongxingwei Launches 12 Production Interconnect Chips, China's First PCIe 6.0 Switch
body: At its October 15 "brand and full-stack product" launch in Wuxi, Chinese interconnect chipmaker Zhongxingwei (众星微) unveiled 12 already-mass-produced high-performance interconnect chips with supporting core IP, plus three next-generation products: a PCIe 6.0 switch, an 800G multi-protocol AI NIC, and a multi-mode RAID chip.

The company frames the AI compute bottleneck as "transport capacity": in large-model training, cluster compute utilization runs as low as just over 20% and at most 53%, while interconnect chips account for 8–9% of system value in GB300- and VR200-class super-nodes. China's first all-domestic 100,000-card compute cluster adopted six Zhongxingwei chips, deploying roughly 200,000 units, with an in-house 32T InfiniBand switch chip paired with 400G NICs handling intra-cluster traffic.

New products include China's first PCIe 6.0 144-lane switch, with native fabric for high-speed XPU interconnect and CXL 3.1 for memory pooling, and a new multi-mode RAID chip whose core throughput is double that of mainstream international rivals. Its storage-interconnect lines (HBA/RAID/SAS Expander) benchmark against overseas leaders across 50 typical workloads.

On quality: 500 servers and 1,000 boards ran 600,000 hours of continuous on-machine testing; chip customer return rates are below 100 DPPM and board returns below 500 DPPM. Ecosystem coverage spans 15+ cloud platforms, 50+ OS variants, 300+ optical-module models and 7 mainstream CPU platforms.

title: Fulin Integrated Raises Nearly ¥1B Series B to Expand InP/GaAs Foundry for AI Optical Modules
body: Putian, Fujian-based compound-semiconductor foundry Fulin Integrated (福联集成, founded 2015) has closed a Series B round of nearly 1 billion yuan, co-led by Shenzhen Capital Group (深创投) and Industrial Securities' investment arm, with Fujian Electronics & Information Group, SMIC Fortune (中芯聚源), a national-level industry fund and others participating. Proceeds will fund phase-two expansion, lifting capacity by more than 50%; the company says it is currently sold out at full utilization.

The round's core draw is its 4-inch indium phosphide (InP) line for optical chips: it has entered the supply chains of the world's top-three optical module makers, serving 800G and next-generation 1.6T modules. Its other line is 6-inch gallium arsenide for RF chips — handset power amplifiers, Wi-Fi front ends, satellite communications — serving tier-one customers at home and abroad.

Market context cited in the coverage: global InP substrate shipments are estimated at about 910,000 wafers in 2025 rising to about 1.28 million in 2027, and Lumentum forecasts an 85% CAGR in AI-driven InP optical-channel shipments. In GaAs foundry, Taiwan's WIN Semiconductors holds over 60% of the merchant market at 43,000 wafers a month, while Sanan IC is China's largest at 18,000 a month; Wi-Fi 7 is lifting PA content per handset from 3–4 to 8–10 units.

The company is listed among Fujian's key IPO-candidate cultivation enterprises, and data from Cailian Press cited in the article puts the probability of follow-on financing within two years at around 77%, signaling clear IPO intent.

title: Changfei Advanced Discloses Diffusion-Bonded SiC Modules, A3-Grade Fab at Baychip Expo
body: At the 2026 Bay Area Semiconductor Industry Ecosystem Expo (Baychip Expo) in Shenzhen, SiC power semiconductor maker Changfei Advanced disclosed fresh progress on high-performance SiC MOSFETs, PCB-embedded packaging and its A3-grade wafer fab, in an interview with Li Gangqun, vice president of its strategic operations center.

The EZ family is China's first power module line built on an advanced diffusion-bonding process, targeting AI data centers (AIDC) and solid-state transformers (SST). Diffusion-bonded joints deliver 2–3x higher bonding strength; the EZ2C cuts junction-to-case thermal resistance by 18% and full-load die junction temperature by more than 25°C, while supporting operation above 200°C. The EZ3C uses an efficient SHB three-level topology to push a single SST module above 100 kW, halving the cascade stages of a 10 kV AI SST system from 16 to 8.

On trench devices, the company started its trench MOSFET patent program in 2023; double-side deep masking/burial techniques plus rounded trench-bottom processing cut trench sidewall roughness (Ra) to 0.15 nm versus 0.7 nm for rivals. As of October 2025 it held 79 public patents in the field, ranking third worldwide; first- and second-generation devices are designated TG1N and TG2N.

Its Wuhan base is the first SiC wafer fab in China to deploy an A3-grade AMHS overhead-transport and dispatch system, with an automatic wafer-start rate above 98% and smart dispatch above 90%. CP yield on 5 mm × 5 mm automotive-grade large dice is stable above 98%, new-product tape-in cycles are 3x faster, and an AI-driven fab utilities system cut overall fab energy use by more than 10.5%.

title: Zhiyuan Robotics Takes Strategic Stake in Tsinghua-Backed RISC-V AI Chip Startup
body: Embodied-intelligence leader Zhiyuan Robotics has taken a strategic stake in Xinji Wuxian (芯际无限), the only RISC-V AI chip company incubated with technology transfer and equity from Tsinghua University. Founded in August 2023, the startup covers the full humanoid-robot stack, from end-effector and motion control to cerebellum and brain-level decision chips.

Its XC64AE series is purpose-built for embodied-intelligence scenarios, with the second-generation XC64AE family slated to complete tape-out in 2027. On the automotive side, the XC32MC body-motor-control MCU is already in mass production in vehicles with aggregate orders exceeding 5 million units; the XC32LS meets the ASIL-D functional-safety grade, recently taped out and powered on, and is now in testing with multiple automakers and Tier-1 suppliers ahead of 2027 mass production; the XC32DC central domain controller integrates an in-house NPU.

The coverage notes that traditional ARM-based automotive chips can carry combined licensing costs of 15–20% of product cost, and that Tsinghua Huakong Technology Transfer Co. took a strategic stake in 2026 via core RISC-V IP. The team is led by founder and CEO Cheng Baozhong and CTO Wei Jian — formerly of Qualcomm, where he led the first in-house GPU and taped out ASIL-D RISC-V cores and automotive cockpit chips.
Zhiyuan, backed by investors including Huawei and Tencent, began its Hong Kong IPO process in July with a targeted valuation of 40–50 billion yuan.

title: Dell CEO Warns AI Server Memory Shortage to Worsen Into 2027
body: Dell Technologies CEO Michael Dell has warned that tight supply of HBM and DRAM will worsen further in 2027, as AI infrastructure demand keeps outpacing global memory capacity growth — making memory the key bottleneck for the AI server industry.
Dell currently sits on a record $95 billion backlog of enterprise and AI server orders, but converting those orders into revenue hinges on securing enough memory chips.

According to The Wall Street Journal, Dell believes the supply constraint could last up to four years, since new fabs take years from planning to full production — much of the added capacity is not expected to be fully online until 2029 or 2030.

To limit risk, Dell runs a lean-inventory model — buying DRAM close to final assembly to avoid tying up working capital — while locking in supply through long-term vendor agreements and customer prepayments.
Rising memory prices are also pushing up manufacturing costs for AI servers and other high-end systems, adding pressure across the AI supply chain.

title: XHEART Closes Strategic Round, Lifetime Funding Reaches ~5 Billion Yuan
body: Chinese physical-AI compute chip startup XHEART (新芯航途) completed a strategic funding round on October 16, bringing its cumulative financing to approximately 5 billion yuan.
Renault Group joined as a first-time investor, Chery Auto increased its stake, and domestic memory leader CXMT (Changxin Memory) also participated in the round.

XHEART builds dedicated compute for edge-side physical-AI models. Its flagship product, the X7 ADAS large-model chip launched in March, uses a dedicated NPU with a hardware-software co-design architecture targeting 200+ TOPS for L2++ urban driving assistance and L3/L4 autonomous driving.

The X7 debuted on the SAIC Volkswagen ID.ERA 9X and is entering the supply systems of SAIC's MG and Roewe brands, GM's Cadillac, and selected Chery models. The company's largest shareholder traces back to Momenta founder Cao Xudong.

title: VTest Wins Approval for 2 Billion Yuan Convertible Bond to Expand High-End Chip Test Capacity
body: Shanghai VTest Semiconductor (伟测科技) has received SSE approval to issue up to 2 billion yuan in convertible bonds, with proceeds earmarked for expanding test capacity for AI compute chips, memory chips, and high-end CIS.

The funds target two projects: the Shanghai HQ base (700 million yuan of the raise) and the Southwest HQ and R&D test base in Chengdu (800 million yuan), both involving new land, facilities, and high-end test equipment.

VTest, a leading third-party IC test house, covers wafer test, final test, SLT, and burn-in for AI chips, CPUs, GPUs, DPUs, SoCs, FPGAs, MCUs, memory, RF, and high-end CIS devices, serving over 200 customers including Unisoc, ZTE Microelectronics, GigaDevice, Fudan Microelectronics, SMIC, Rockchip, and Novosense.

The company reported H1 2026 revenue of 1.072 billion yuan, up 69% year on year, with net profit of 159 million yuan, up 57.6%, driven by high-end test demand from AI compute, smart driving, and large-capacity memory chips.
This is VTest's second straight year of convertible-bond financing, following an 1.175 billion yuan issue in April 2025 that was redeemed in March 2026 after a share-price rally.

title: Jialichuang Plans Hong Kong Listing Less Than Three Months After A-Share Debut
body: Jialichuang (嘉立创, 001232) announced plans to issue H shares and list on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange main board — less than three months after its A-share debut on August 4, when its shares peaked above 234 yuan and market value once exceeded 130 billion yuan.

The company, a one-stop electronics-industry service provider covering PCB manufacturing, electronic component distribution, and assembly, says the listing would support its globalization strategy, widen offshore financing channels, and strengthen its overseas brand.

Overseas revenue grew 63.76% year on year to 1.516 billion yuan in H1 2026, accounting for 21.14% of total revenue. The company also guided Q1–Q3 2026 net profit to rise 78.76%–118.48% year on year, partly on overseas growth.
In the same roundup, Dongshan Precision received CSRC filing approval to issue up to 234,038,600 H shares for a Hong Kong listing, moving its IPO process to the HKEX hearing and pricing stage.

title: Changfei Advanced Launches SiC MOSFET Series, New Power Modules at Shenzhen Tech Event
body: SiC power semiconductor maker Changfei Advanced, founded in May 2022, held a "Everest Summit" technology launch in Shenzhen on October 15, unveiling its high-performance SiC MOSFET series PG4E/PG5E/PG6N, E2Drive automotive main-drive power modules, DeepXE embedded-PCB power modules, and EZ2C/3C — described as China's first diffusion-welded SiC power modules — alongside new products for AI data centers, industrial, and consumer markets.

The company said its portfolio has grown from zero to 131 products, with process cell size shrunk from 5.8μm to 2.8μm, a 575-person R&D team, and combined annual capacity of 420,000 SiC wafers across its Wuhan and Wuhu fabs. Wuhan is billed as the SiC industry's first A3-level smart wafer fab, with MOSFET production cycle of about 40 days and over 98% CP yield on 5×5mm chips.

On specs: the 1200V PG4E posts room-temperature Rsp of 2.2 mΩ·cm² (4.4 mΩ·cm² at 175°C), 2.1μs short-circuit withstand (27% above rivals), and 11.2% higher avalanche energy. The PG5E cuts room-temperature Rsp to 1.9 mΩ·cm² (about 13.5% below the prior generation) with 30% better short-circuit withstand versus competitors, while the PG6N reaches 1.7 mΩ·cm² Rsp and supports operation up to 200–225°C.

For modules: the E2Dmini-J, co-developed with Jingwei HiRain, delivers 540 Arms peak current (20% above the 450 Arms industry level) with 36% lower stray inductance. DeepXE's embedded-PCB module gets stray inductance down to 0.9 nH (75% below conventional packaging), 20% higher current density, 15% lower thermal resistance, and halves size and weight — 24 SiC MOSFETs on a poker-card-sized footprint reaching 250 kW peak. The diffusion-welded EZ2C/3C replaces tin-based solder (melting point ~500°C vs 230°C) with 2–3x bond strength and thermal conductivity, cutting case-to-sink thermal resistance by 18% and full-load junction temperature by over 25°C; EZ3C pushes a single SST module from 70 kW to over 100 kW and halves 10 kV AI SST cascade stages from 16 to 8.

Automotive SiC chips now number 50-plus models with over 20 million units shipped at a claimed 0 PPM quality record; consumer products span 38 models (650V–800V) with over 100 million units shipped, and industrial products 93 models (650V–3300V) with 15 million shipped. For data centers, its 800V HVDC lineup targets PSU cabinets of 18 kW/30 kW at over 98.5% efficiency and 40–80 kW SST modules. On the trench-MOS roadmap, the first-generation TG1N (1200V, 11 mΩ) is in mass production; the second generation shrinks cell size 27% and on-resistance 16% (mass production in 2026), with a third generation at 1.5μm cell and 1.3 mΩ·cm² Rsp slated for 2027 — an Incopat search put its 79 trench-MOS public patents (Oct 2024–Oct 2025) third worldwide behind Fuji Electric (139) and Infineon (109). The article cites a 2025 global SiC power semiconductor market of about $2.79 billion, projected to reach $21.58 billion by 2034 at 25.52% CAGR.

title: China's DF1000 AI Chip Adapts 130B-Parameter Model Training Pipeline in 7 Days
body: Domestic AI-chip startup Dongfang Suanxin said its DF1000 processor, launched in July, completed a full bring-up from chip to cluster in a short period and adapted the training pipeline of the Step 130B large model in just 7 days — clarified as getting operators, distributed links, and cluster scheduling working so training could start, not a complete from-scratch training run of the 130B model.

The DF1000 uses a software-defined chip architecture whose compute arrays and interconnect can be dynamically switched between data movement, tensor, and vector compute without a respin, and a 3D hybrid-bonded near-memory compute design with logic and DRAM wafers vertically stacked, copper-to-copper direct bonding, and sub-micron interconnect pitch.

Measured figures: 520 TFLOPS of BF16 compute at 14nm, 6.4 TB/s memory bandwidth, and 900 GB/s scale-up interconnect bandwidth — over 5x the memory bandwidth of a conventional HBM setup at the same capacity. The software stack supports PyTorch, Megatron-LM, vLLM, Triton, Kubernetes, Hugging Face, and SGLang, with LLaMA, DeepSeek, and Qwen models claimed to work out of the box.
VP Guo Wei said at the DF1000 launch that the chip's goal is to fix real bottlenecks in large-model training and inference, not to look good on a few spec parameters.

title: China's FPGA Vendors Push High-End Launches in 2026, Review Says
body: Chinese FPGA vendors are moving from entry-level "drop-in replacements" to original high-end innovation in 2026, according to an October 18 industry review on eefocus, which points to four shifts: Physical AI going mainstream, FPGA Agent intelligent development, Chiplet packaging breakthroughs, and volume ramp of domestic high-end products.

In high-end compute, Pango Microsystems' Titan-3 series is described as China's top mass-produced general FPGA, delivering 1,300K LUTs of logic capacity with DDR5 and PCIe 3.0, targeting 5G/6G communications, data-center acceleration, and high-speed image codecs. For edge AI, Fudan Microelectronics' new AI heterogeneous computing platform combines CPU, FPGA, and an in-house NPU for the edge deployment of 70B-class models, with its FMZQ400TAI part rated at 128 TOPS INT8 peak.

In automotive, Anlogic's Phoenix PH1P series passed AEC-Q100 Grade 2 qualification, among the few domestic high-end FPGAs that can ship in cars in volume. Efinix's 16nm Titanium series pairs a Quantum variable-logic architecture with PCIe Gen4 and 16 Gbps SerDes for low-power, high-speed interconnect such as optical communications and high-speed backplanes.

The review also notes smarter domestic EDA tooling lowering the development barrier: Pango's PDS tool is positioned against Xilinx Vivado with SystemVerilog support, and all major domestic vendors now ship AI-assisted development flows for auto-routing, timing closure, and bug triage.

title: Japan Approves TSMC's 3nm Plan for Kumamoto Fab Two, Targeting 6,000 Wafers a Month
body: Japan's Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry on October 16 approved TSMC's plan to produce 3nm advanced semiconductors at its second Kumamoto fab, which would be the first 3nm chip manufacturing on Japanese soil.

The fab was originally slated for 6nm and 12nm processes at 48,000 wafers per month plus 40nm capacity; the new plan sets 3nm output at 6,000 wafers per month, with METI saying the sharp capacity cut reflects the shift to higher-performance products. The approval covers the fab's first phase, and TSMC plans to add capacity with further government support.
METI also approved changes at the operating first Kumamoto fab: 12–16nm production will be discontinued, and 22–28nm capacity will be trimmed from 55,000 to 45,000 wafers per month.
Japanese media report the switch to 3nm reflects rising AI demand, and Nikkei confirmed the new 3nm plant has been approved for subsidies.

title: Shanghai OSAT Xiangxin Integrated Circuits Declared Bankrupt
body: The Shanghai Third Intermediate People's Court on October 15 declared Shanghai Xiangxin Integrated Circuits Co. bankrupt (case (2025) Hu 03 Po No. 918), ruling the company cannot pay its due debts and its assets are insufficient to cover them; the court had accepted the bankruptcy liquidation application on September 19, 2025.

Founded in November 2011, Xiangxin focused on power-management IC packaging and testing, building SOP and SOT lines covering wafer thinning, dicing, wire bonding, molding, metal surface treatment, trimming and final test, with total investment of RMB 60 million.
Its packaging services supplied chipmakers including Wuxi Chipown, with products going into consumer electronics and industrial control applications.
The ruling adds another bankruptcy case to China's intensely competitive OSAT sector, where many smaller packagers are under pressure.

title: Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan: US-China Chip Gap "Not That Big"
body: In a Tokyo interview in early October, Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan said the US government's minority stake in Intel has no impact on the company's governance and does not affect its commercial strategy, and that Intel's restructuring is 80% complete.
He credited government backing for enabling long-term investment in a competitive foundry business, citing TSMC's decade-plus journey to chipmaking leadership.

On China's semiconductor progress, Tan said US and Chinese firms "each have their own strengths and weaknesses," and when asked whether Chinese chipmaking could catch up within five to ten years, replied: "as things stand, I don't think the gap is that big."

title: Huawei: 2027 Kirin Chip in Testing, Results "As Expected"
body: At a Kirin chip technology briefing at Huawei's Shanghai Lianqihu R&D center on October 13 — its first dedicated Kirin event in six years — Huawei said it systematically reviewed the mass-production progress of its "logic folding" technology.
The company also disclosed that its next-generation Kirin chip, expected in 2027, has entered testing, with results meeting expectations.

title: China's Equipment Trio Rushes Into Hybrid Bonding: Tuojing's RMB 2.5 Billion Deal Leads
body: On the evening of October 15, Tuojing Technology and NAURA both disclosed acquisition plans targeting hybrid bonding equipment; three days earlier, AMEC's subsidiary announced a capital injection of up to RMB 35 million into bonding firm Qinghe Jingyuan — three major domestic chip-equipment makers moving on the same track within days.

Tuojing Technology plans to acquire 82.97% of Wuxi Shangji plus 100% each of Wuxi Kuanghang and Shanghai Tainawei for RMB 2.5 billion via shares and cash, raising up to RMB 1.82 billion in supporting funds alongside. Wuxi Shangji, a PVD and etching equipment maker, committed to revenues of no less than RMB 350 million, 450 million and 610 million for 2026–2028. After the deal, Tuojing will offer a complete 3D-integration equipment product line covering thin-film deposition, etching, bonding and metrology, enabling one-stop procurement and joint process development for customers.

NAURA's subsidiary will acquire hybrid-bonding equipment maker Nuohe Jianwei for RMB 405 million in cash. Nuohe's tools have already reached nanometer-level alignment precision, secured repeat orders, and are awaiting validation by leading customers.

Hybrid bonding, called the "chokepoint process" of 3D chips, is entering a fast landing phase, with related equipment demand expected to multiply by 2030, driven by the explosive growth of AI/HPC and HBM. Dutch firm BESI still holds about 70% of the global market, but Chinese equipment makers are accelerating their catch-up from zero to one, shifting competition from single-tool breakthroughs to platform-based turnkey solutions.

title: Galaxy Microelectronics to Acquire Hengtaike for RMB 645 Million in Power-Device Push
body: Galaxy Microelectronics (688689.SH) announced after market close on October 16 that it plans to acquire 100% of Hengtaike Semiconductor (Shanghai) for RMB 645 million through share issuance, and will raise supporting funds of up to RMB 580.5 million for the industrialization of high-reliability medium/high-voltage MOS device packaging projects.

The deal values the transaction at RMB 28.24 per share, involving about 22.84 million new shares. Hengtaike is a national-level "Little Giant" company specializing in power semiconductor products for construction machinery, drones, photovoltaics and energy storage, with industry-leading medium-voltage SGT MOSFET and high-voltage Super Junction technology.

In the 150V–200V range, Hengtaike's medium/high-voltage SGT MOSFETs are said to match the product lines of international leading vendors. The transaction values Hengtaike's equity at RMB 586 million under the income approach, a 139.63% premium.

Galaxy Microelectronics, which focuses on semiconductor discrete devices with an IDM model, concentrates its power-device portfolio in the low-voltage segment. The acquisition aims to quickly fill its medium/high-voltage gap and accelerate the iteration of automotive-grade devices and new product launches, following the company's September announcement of a RMB 1.078 billion capacity expansion project.

title: Xingfu Electronic to Raise Up to RMB 260 Million for 40,000-Ton Semiconductor-Grade Phosphoric Acid Project
body: Xingfu Electronic (688545.SH) announced it plans to issue shares under a simplified procedure to raise no more than RMB 260 million, with the net proceeds fully funding a 40,000-ton-per-year electronic-grade phosphoric acid project; total project investment is RMB 480 million.
The move is aimed at consolidating its leading position in electronic-grade phosphoric acid, a key wet-chemical material used in chip manufacturing.

title: Fujian Huaqing Takes China's No.1 and World's No.2 Spot in Aluminum Nitride Ceramic Substrates
body: According to YHResearch's "Global Aluminum Nitride (AlN) Ceramic Substrate Market Report 2025-2031", Fujian Huaqing Electronic Materials Technology Co., Ltd. has surpassed several established international giants to rank first in China and second globally by AlN ceramic substrate market share.

AlN ceramics are a core base material for the power semiconductor industry — prized for high thermal conductivity, high temperature tolerance, high resistivity and low dielectric loss — serving as key heat-dissipation and packaging substrates for IGBTs and large-scale integrated circuits across 5G communications, photovoltaics, energy storage, rail transit and automotive electronics.

The company, a national "Little Giant" firm and China's first professional high-thermal-conductivity AlN ceramics manufacturer, attributes the breakthrough to in-house high-purity ceramic powder synthesis — ending dependence on imported premium powders — plus full-chain processes from tape casting and high-temperature sintering to precision grinding and etching, solving the industry's high-end AlN mass-production challenge.

Its products cover powder, substrates, copper-clad laminates and precision ceramic structural parts, and have won recognition from leading customers upstream and downstream worldwide, marking another domestic substitution milestone in a long-overseas-dominated key material.

title: SEMI Sees 300mm Fab Equipment Spending Hitting US$227 Billion by 2029
body: SEMI's 300mm Fab Outlook report forecasts global 300mm front-end fab equipment spending at US$149 billion in 2026, up 31% year on year, staying in double-digit growth to reach US$227 billion by 2029. Americas-region investment is projected to climb from US$18.1 billion in 2026 to US$40.6 billion in 2029.

IDC data shows Nvidia's share of China's data-center AI chip market fell to 34% in the first half of 2026, with shipments of 678,000 accelerators, down 44% year on year. Huawei shipped 572,000 AI accelerators, up roughly 90%, taking 28% of the market. Of the 11 Chinese chipmakers IDC tracks, nine grew shipments year on year; total China AI accelerator shipments reached 2.008 million units, and IDC expects 19% growth for the full year.

Counterpoint Research's preliminary data shows global Q3 smartphone shipments down 20% year on year — a 14-year Q3 low — as rising DRAM and NAND prices pushed up retail prices by 20% this year. Samsung held 23% share to stay number one, while Apple reached 22%, its first time above 20% in a third quarter.

Wuxi-based Zhongxingwei, a relatively low-profile domestic interconnect chipmaker that has spent six years on the segment, held a brand and full-stack product launch where it presented its full-scenario high-performance interconnect chip platform for the first time.

The lineup spans general-compute interconnect — HBA cards, RAID cards, RoCE NICs and PCIe switch chips for server and storage systems — and AI-compute interconnect, including PCIe switches, 400G InfiniBand NICs and IB switches. The company also launched three self-developed new chips: the C82-4G, described as China's first PCIe 6.0 switch (up to 144 lanes at 64 GT/s per lane, doubling PCIe 5.0 bandwidth), an 800G multi-protocol AI NIC, also described as a domestic first, and a multi-mode RAID chip supporting SAS, SATA and PCIe 5.0 with a built-in hardware encryption engine.

Zhongxingwei says cumulative shipments have exceeded 800,000 units, with over 400,000 units shipped in 2025 alone and revenue surpassing 1 billion yuan. Its products are in use at Inspur, Lenovo, H3C and ZTE, and it signed strategic cooperation agreements with seven industry partners — Kylinsoft, UnionTech, Tencent Cloud, Inspur, H3C, ZTE and Lenovo.
title: Chinese Interconnect Chipmaker Zhongxingwei Unveils Full-Stack Platform, Tops 800,000 Units Shipped

body: At CIIF 2026, Chinese chipmaker Axera launched the AX8860 series of large-compute edge AI SoCs, targeting industrial intelligence as AI moves from the cloud to the physical world. The series includes the AX8860 and AX8860P, positioned as compute platforms 'born for physical AI.'

Built on a 6nm process after 15 months of development, the chips deliver up to 256 TOPS with mixed-precision compute and are among the industry's first edge chips natively supporting FP4 precision. Each chip carries 273 GB/s of memory bandwidth and natively supports 128GB of LPDDR5X; a built-in AXLink chip-to-chip interface enables dual- and quad-chip cascading with memory pooling, reaching 512GB of memory with four chips — enough to run models above 100 billion parameters, such as DeepSeek V4 Flash, at the edge.

Axera says early AX8860P tests show prefill and decode speeds matching leading international flagship GPUs, while full-load power consumption is only 45% of the competitor's, with multi-chip cascading efficiency holding around 80%. The launch is accompanied by four hardware forms: the A256S core module, PCIe inference cards (single, dual and quad-chip; the quad-chip card offers roughly 1000 TOPS and a 512GB memory pool), the Agentic Box, and edge inference servers.
title: Axera Launches AX8860 Edge AI SoC Series for Industrial 'Physical AI'

body: Chinese RISC-V server-chip startup Ruisixin has closed a new funding round with Renjun Capital and Shuimu Fund participating, according to a report (amount undisclosed). The team comes from the original Berkeley RISC-V project group, and founder Tan Zhangxi studied under RISC-V co-founder David Patterson.

The round caps a dense financing streak across the sector: Lanxin Computing closed a Series B of nearly 2 billion yuan with 18 investors last month, Lingrui Zhixin raised several hundred million yuan in July, and last year Jindie Shikong, Chaorui Technology and Yuefang Technology each closed nine-figure rounds. Overseas, Tenstorrent raised a $693 million Series D.

Policy support is also crystallizing: the 15th Five-Year Plan for electronic information manufacturing issued by MIIT and NDRC lists 'advancing 5th-generation RISC (RISC-V) R&D and industrialization' — the first time RISC-V has appeared as a task item in a national five-year plan. The article notes industry-wide consolidation may be next, as competition shifts from single demos to ecosystem completeness and real deployments.
title: RISC-V Funding Wave: Ruisixin Closes New Round as Sector Eyes Consolidation

body: Chinese AI cloud-compute chip startup Suanmiao Technology announced it has closed its Pre-A2 and A funding rounds, bringing its total fundraising over the past year to nearly 2 billion yuan, according to the report.

The company focuses on R&D and volume production of large-compute AI cloud chips built on a 3D architecture. It says proceeds are earmarked for three priorities: recruiting top R&D talent, doubling down on core-technology iteration, and accelerating the mass-production ramp of its self-developed 3D TokenPU large-model compute chip.
Rather than following the conventional GPU route, Suanmiao is betting its 3D chip architecture can carve out a differentiated path in AI inference compute.
title: 3D-Architecture AI Chip Startup Suanmiao Raises Nearly 2 Billion Yuan in a Year

body: Sanan Optoelectronics (600703.SH) disclosed on the evening of October 15 that creditors Hubei Changjiang Anxin Industry Investment Fund and Hunan Lugu Development Group applied to the Xiamen Intermediate People's Court for bankruptcy restructuring of controlling shareholder Xiamen Sanan Electronics; Hunan Lugu Development Group also filed against indirect controlling shareholder Fujian Sanan Group.
The court has issued notices for both applications but had not formally accepted them as of the announcement date, so whether the companies enter restructuring remains uncertain.

The two shareholders together hold 1.312 billion shares, or 26.30% of total share capital, of which 794 million shares (60.52%) are pledged; all 1.312 billion shares are judicially frozen, with cumulative round-robin freezes of 8.213 billion shares — 625.89% of their holdings and 164.63% of total share capital.

The company said operations remain normal; H1 2026 revenue was RMB 6.468 billion, down 28.04% year-on-year, with a net loss of RMB 97.9 million. Founder Lin Xiucheng was placed under criminal detention on September 24 on suspicion of embezzlement and misappropriation of funds.
Sanan closed at RMB 10.78 on October 15, down 3.66%, for a market cap of about RMB 54.1 billion. This follows an earlier June 2026 filing by creditor Lin Suzhen, which was withdrawn in September.
title: Sanan Optoelectronics' Controlling Shareholders Face New Bankruptcy-Restructuring Filings

body: GlobalFoundries announced on October 14 that it was selected as technology provider and operator for two new 300mm fabs at its Malta, New York site, fully funded by US$21 billion of Japanese investment — the first major semiconductor manufacturing project under the US-Japan trade and investment framework.
Funding flows from the July 22, 2025 US-Japan agreement under which Japan committed US$550 billion in US investment with tariffs capped at 15%.

About US$10 billion will accelerate the first fab, targeting groundbreaking in Q4 2026, tool-install readiness in 2028, and first wafers in 2029; another roughly US$10 billion supports the second fab.

At full capacity the two fabs add roughly 1.8 million 300mm wafers per year, lifting total US wafer capacity by about 10%, and are projected to create some 27,000 construction and ecosystem jobs plus over 1,000 skilled manufacturing jobs.

GlobalFoundries itself puts up no capital: the US and Japanese governments will hold the plants and equipment through an SPV, while GF earns construction, operating, and licensing fees; CFO Sam Franklin expects about US$3 billion of cumulative free cash flow over ten years from the first fab and long-term EPS accretion of US$0.50 to US$0.75.

The US Commerce Department will reallocate US$955 million of CHIPS and Science Act funding to accelerate GF's silicon photonics, silicon-germanium, and advanced packaging investments in Malta and Burlington, Vermont, and separately takes about 4% equity in GlobalFoundries.
Endorsements came from Renesas CEO Hidetoshi Shibata, Apple COO Sabih Khan (on the back of Apple's US$600 billion US investment pledge), GM President Mark Reuss, Lynx Logic, and Tokyo Electron.
title: Japan to Fund US$21 Billion Twin 300mm Fabs in New York, GlobalFoundries to Operate Them

body: Lumentum CEO Michael Hurlston told Bloomberg on October 9 that the company's optical components for AI servers are completely sold out through early 2029 — the company cannot meet about 70% of demand for some products through 2027 or about 30% for others through 2028, a full year worse than its sell-out-by-2028 forecast six months ago.
Nvidia invested US$2 billion in Lumentum (and rival Coherent) earlier this year; analysts expect Lumentum's sales to more than double this year.
FY2026 Q4 revenue hit US$1.01 billion, up 109% year-on-year, and electro-absorption modulated laser (EML) shipments are expected to grow over 50% in the December 2026 quarter.
New capacity takes three to five years to build; Lumentum is expanding InP wafer plants in Japan, and its Greensboro, North Carolina facility is expected to start contributing revenue in early 2028.
The supply crunch could worsen if the US curbs Chinese optical transceivers: Counterpoint Research says Lumentum and Coherent could not fill a gap left by Chinese makers such as Innolight.
title: Lumentum's AI Optical Parts Sold Out Through Early 2029

body: Inverter maker Deye Technology (Ningbo Deye Technology) said at its October 10, 2026 global supplier conference that 2027 procurement will exceed RMB 18 billion, a 2024–2027 compound annual growth rate of 66.8%, covering cells, magnetic components, power devices, capacitors, resistors, ICs, PCBs, and more.

It targets 680,000 inverters per month and 600,000 energy-storage battery packs per month of capacity for 2027; cumulative global shipments have topped 9 million units, with 1.153 million inverters sold in H1 2026.
H1 2026 inverter revenue was about RMB 5.13 billion, up 94.09% year-on-year, representing 48.36% of main business revenue.

Deye disclosed it is moving its inverters from traditional silicon to third-generation silicon carbide: its sixth-generation SG06 home storage inverters already use SiC heavily, and 1.25–5MW expandable solid-state transformer solutions under development may adopt SiC too.
Its SiC supply chain already spans Sanan Semiconductor, LINGRUI Semi, PineSemi, Huarun Micro, Wolfspeed, and others; LINGRUI and PineSemi received "frontier innovation" awards at the event.
title: Deye Plans Over ¥18 Billion of 2027 Procurement as Inverters Shift to SiC

body: The FCC's Report and Order FCC 26-50 took effect October 13, 2026 (adopted July 22, published in the Federal Register September 11), extending US equipment-authorization bans from finished devices to components.

Any device containing logic hardware components made by entities on the FCC "covered list" can no longer receive FCC equipment authorization if the finished device made by that entity would itself be denied — effectively blocking it from the US market.

The "logic hardware component" definition covers digital components generating or using timing signals at over 9,000 pulses per second — essentially all programmable devices including CPUs, SoCs, FPGAs, and Wi-Fi/Bluetooth modules; passive components are excluded.

E-commerce platforms are pulled into enforcement: participation in consignment, warehousing, or order processing counts as "marketing"; self-operated or controlled product pages must display valid FCC IDs by March 1, 2027, and third-party pages must complete reasonable FCC ID verification by June 1, 2027.
FCC Chair Brendan Carr called the move "completely closing the component loophole"; the legal basis includes the Secure Equipment Act of 2021 and Section 889 of the FY2019 NDAA.
title: FCC Rule Now Bans Devices Containing Huawei/ZTE Logic Components
ByteDance Reportedly Nears Deal for MediaTek's Custom AI ASICs
body: Bloomberg reported on Oct 14, citing people familiar with the matter, that ByteDance is close to reaching an agreement to buy customized data-center semiconductors from MediaTek. The ASICs would be tailored for ByteDance's platforms, with the purchase quantity undisclosed; if the deal closes, ByteDance could become MediaTek's second-largest customer for this class of chips after Google.

Neither company confirmed the talks: ByteDance did not immediately comment, and MediaTek declined to comment. The report also said MediaTek expects about $2 billion in AI-chip sales in 2026 and aims to capture 15% of an estimated $80 billion market next year.

The deal would land as ByteDance ramps AI spending — its 2026 capital expenditure is estimated at more than 200 billion yuan (about $29.4 billion), with roughly half earmarked for advanced semiconductors, alongside plans for test orders of 20,000 Nvidia H200 GPUs at roughly $20,000 apiece.

title: ASML Studies Further 2028 Capacity Boost as Q3 Sales Hit Record €11.7 Billion
body: ASML posted record quarterly net sales of €11.7 billion for Q3 2026 on Oct 14 — up 25% from Q2's €9.3 billion and 55% from a year earlier — with a gross margin of 57.5% and net income of €5 billion. The company guided full-year 2026 net sales to €44–45 billion, about 36% higher than 2025, at roughly 56% gross margin, and said China should account for about 20% of its business.

CEO Christophe Fouquet said the company's planned capacity for 2027 and 2028 still cannot fully satisfy customer demand, so ASML is studying a further expansion of 2028 output. The company expects to deliver about 65 EUV systems in 2026 — more than 50% above last year — while immersion DUV shipments stay roughly flat.

Fouquet added that customers see the supply shortage lasting at least through 2028: new orders for 2028 have jumped sharply, and some customers have already opened talks for 2029 and 2030. He also confirmed that TSMC and ASML broadly agree on introducing High-NA EUV into volume production around 2030.

title: Guangzhou Foundry CanSemi Jumps 274.69% on ChiNext Debut
body: CanSemi (粤芯半导体), dubbed "Guangzhou's No. 1 chip company," listed on the Shenzhen ChiNext board on Oct 13 — the first pure wafer-manufacturing company on the board. It priced at 12.01 yuan per share, issued 513 million shares and raised 6.157 billion yuan gross, then opened at 45 yuan per share — up 274.69% — for a market capitalization of about 130 billion yuan.

Founded in December 2017 in Guangzhou's Huangpu district, the company is the Greater Bay Area's first 12-inch wafer maker in volume production. It focuses on specialty analog and mixed-signal processes from 180nm to 55nm — MS, HV, CIS, BCD, eNVM, MOSFET, IGBT and SiPho — and, per Frost & Sullivan, is mainland China's only company with mass-production capability on a 12-inch silicon-photonics platform, with more than 7,000 SiPho wafers taped out by September 15, 2026.

Its first two fabs are planned for 80,000 wafers per month (63,300 reached by end-2025) and should approach 120,000 wpm after the phase-3 project. 2025 capacity utilization ran at 96.38% with a 99.47% sell-through rate. Revenue grew from 1.044 billion yuan in 2023 to 2.582 billion in 2025 (a 57.3% CAGR), but cumulative three-year losses exceeded 6.5 billion yuan, and the company targets breakeven no earlier than 2029.

title: Silicon-Photonics Maker Xihe Clears SSE Review, Seeks 1.83 Billion Yuan IPO
body: Shanghai Xihe Technology Co., Ltd. (羊禾科技) cleared its SSE review on Oct 14, according to the exchange's website. The national "little giant" plans to raise 1.83 billion yuan to industrialize silicon-photonic ICs for AI compute and data centers, develop next-generation chips and build an R&D center.

Founded in 2021 in Shanghai's Putuo district, Xihe makes high-performance silicon-photonic integrated chips covering 400G, 800G and 1.6T rates, and is expanding into 3.2T and 6.4T NPO/CPO transceiver chips. Its products sit in the supply chains of major international optical-module makers and are deployed in AI clusters and hyperscale data centers.

Cumulative shipments topped 12 million chips by August 2026 — one of very few vendors worldwide at that scale — and Frost & Sullivan puts its 2025 global market share at about 13%. The company held 3.279 billion yuan in backorders at the end of H1 2026, with 800G products making up 47.57%.

title: SIA Report: America's 95% "Safe" Chip Supply Chain Is a Mirage
body: The U.S. Semiconductor Industry Association, together with McKinsey, has published a new report, "Understanding Dependencies in the U.S. Semiconductor Supply Chain," that punctures the industry's sense of security. By company headquarters, 95% of the roughly $27 billion in equipment and materials the U.S. chip ecosystem consumes each year comes from suppliers based in the U.S., Europe or Japan — but measured by actual production location, that share falls to 68%, with the portion made in mainland China, Israel, Southeast Asia, South Korea and Taiwan jumping from 5% to 32%.

The report rates about 11% of Tier 1 supply categories as "high vulnerability" and 38% as medium — roughly half in total. And once sub-tier dependencies are included, more than three-quarters of Tier 1 categories depend on at least one high-risk upstream input.

Stark examples: mainland China supplies about 40% of the world's xenon and krypton (critical for lithography) and about 35% of tungsten, plus roughly 95% of gallium and electronic-grade polysilicon; Japan provides about 75% of ABF substrates and 70% of mask blanks. The report urges targeted incentives, strategic stockpiles and deeper coordination with allied supply chains rather than wholesale reshoring.

title: Domestic EUV Light Source Prototype Debuts, Mass Production Seen in 3-5 Years
body: Langdao Suiyan (Shanghai) Technology publicly unveiled its self-developed extreme ultraviolet (EUV) light source system prototype at the 26th China International Industry Fair — described as the most advanced domestically disclosed EUV light source prototype in China to date.

The company claims a 90% localization rate, with nearly all core components independently designed, developed, and manufactured, and says it follows the same mainstream technology route as leading international vendors.

For its FlintNano LPP-OXXO low-power EUV light source, the company disclosed full core parameters: drive laser power up to 1,000 W, laser frequency of 1-20 kHz, photoelectric conversion efficiency above 2%, brightness of 100 W/mm²sr, stable EUV output above 15 W, and continuous operation exceeding 100 hours.

Plasma working size is controlled at 60 μm, with plasma stability error within 3% RMS and overall energy output stability error of 5%. The high-power FlintMicro-LPP line has completed principle verification, while the low-power FlintNano-LPP series has entered commercialization.

Founded in 2024 as a Tsinghua University spin-off led by Dr. Wang Hao, the company has raised tens of millions of yuan in total and closed a Series A round this July with semiconductor industry capital on board.
Company engineers said 3 to 5 years of engineering work are still needed before scaled mass production, with output-power scaling and long-term operational stability as the two core challenges.

title: CXMT's 4F² DRAM Architecture Breakthrough Triggers Global Memory Stock Sell-Off
body: ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) announced key progress on its next-generation 4F² DRAM cell architecture and plans to ship a server DDR5 RDIMM product combining the architecture with hybrid bonding by the end of 2026.

The news broke the market's consensus that high-end memory would stay in structural shortage, triggering a cross-market sell-off around October 13: SK Hynix plunged 10.09% in a single day, Samsung fell 7.39%, dragging the KOSPI down more than 6% intraday and tripping a circuit breaker.
Micron dropped more than 4%, SanDisk fell nearly 6-7%, Seagate and Western Digital also slid, while Kioxia closed down over 13%.

The disruptive point is CXMT's self-developed vertical surrounding-gate (VSG) transistor structure, which shrinks the planar area of a single memory cell by about one-third and lifts theoretical storage density by roughly 50%, significantly lowering cost per bit at the same wafer and node.

Samsung's own target is mass production of sub-10nm 4F² DRAM in 2028, and SK Hynix only published its 4F² roadmap in 2025 — if CXMT delivers by year-end, it would hold roughly a two-year architecture-level lead.

According to HSBC, CXMT's global DRAM revenue share has climbed from about 4% a year ago to roughly 10% now, and the market fears scaled low-cost production in conventional server DRAM could undercut the incumbents' supply-discipline pricing model.
Analysts cautioned the breakthrough won't immediately shake Samsung and SK Hynix's HBM dominance, with volume yield, unit cost, and major server-customer qualification as the key tests ahead.

title: DigiKey Becomes First Distributor for TDK SensEI's edgeRX Starter
body: DigiKey announced a distribution agreement with TDK SensEI, becoming the first distributor of the edgeRX Starter predictive-maintenance (PdM) solution, which is now available on DigiKey.cn.

The solution combines AI-driven multimodal sensing with advanced analytics to turn vibration and temperature data into early warnings of equipment issues, helping users spot failure patterns and receive predictive insights and guided recommendations.

Jason Simoneau, DigiKey's vice president of Passive Devices and Multi-Market Semiconductors, said DigiKey teams already use the solution in their own product fulfillment centers and have seen real benefits.

TDK SensEI CEO Sandeep Pandya said edgeRX Starter is designed to lower the barrier to predictive maintenance so industrial teams of all sizes — including those with limited resources or in-house expertise — can deploy advanced AI-driven maintenance.

TDK SensEI (Sensor Edge Intelligence) fuses TDK's sensor systems, software design, and machine learning expertise, with hardware spanning motion, magnetic, microphone, and current sensors plus temperature and battery/energy-harvesting solutions.

title: Global Electronics Association Publishes IPC-1783-CO2E Carbon Footprint Data Standard
body: The Global Electronics Association (formerly IPC) officially released IPC-1783-CO2E, an international standard for collecting and reporting CO2-equivalent (CO2e) emissions data across the electronics manufacturing supply chain.

The standard aims to improve the consistency, credibility, and comparability of product carbon footprint data, addressing the industry's long-standing problem of inconsistent measurement, estimation, collection, and reporting methods.

Francis D'Souza, chair of the IPC-1783-CO2E technical committee and CEO of banyan.eco, said the standard provides a practical, standardized measurement and reporting method together with data quality indicators.

It helps companies build standardized data methods, support product-level CO2e accounting through activity and process models, strengthen data quality with appropriate methodologies and quality indicators, and stay aligned with the GHG Protocol and relevant ISO principles.

The standard targets professionals in sustainability, environmental compliance, supply chain, procurement, manufacturing, and product management, and the association says it lays a common foundation for reliable product carbon footprint data.

title: AMEC Founder Warns of AI Bubble, Predicts 90% of China's Equipment Vendors Face Elimination
body: Yin Zhiyao, founder, chairman and general manager of AMEC (Advanced Micro-Fabrication Equipment), warned in a keynote at the CIIF integrated-circuit summit on October 12 that the AI investment frenzy could turn into a bubble, and that China's semiconductor equipment industry is headed for massive consolidation.

He pointed to a telling gap: chip production sales have nearly doubled, up close to 100%, while the semiconductor equipment industry grew only 17%. Reviewing global semiconductor capex cycles from 1984 to 2026, he noted swings from 100% annual growth to 30% declines, with each boom historically driven by a single product wave — and AI's turn, he said, 'has not fully arrived.'

China has an estimated 500 to 1,000 semiconductor equipment vendors, Yin said, while the US consolidated down to just dozens. If China follows the same path, 90% of domestic equipment makers could be eliminated, he argued, calling an end to 'scattered, guerrilla-style development.'

AMEC disclosed its standing in etch, the largest equipment segment at roughly $22 billion globally in 2025: Lam Research holds about 45%, Tokyo Electron 16–28% and Applied Materials 16–27%, with the top three taking about 90%, while AMEC ranks fourth worldwide at 3–6%. Domestically it holds over 60% of the CCP etch market and over 40% of ICP etch, reaches 28% in domestic 12-inch advanced fabs, and is the only Chinese equipment vendor in the 5nm supply chain.

For 2025 AMEC reported revenue of about 12.385 billion yuan, up 36.62%, net profit of about 2.111 billion yuan, up 30.69%, and R&D spending of 3.744 billion yuan, roughly 30% of revenue. The company plans to develop 100 tool types over the next three to five years with 13 billion yuan in R&D, targeting over 60% domestic IC equipment coverage by 2030.

title: FCC to Vote on Barring Chinese Labs from Testing US Electronics
body: The US Federal Communications Commission announced it will hold a final vote on October 29 on its 'third report and order.' If passed, testing labs and telecom certification bodies (TCBs) located in countries without a mutual recognition agreement (MRA) with the US would lose FCC recognition starting December 1, 2028 — and mainland China is not on the reciprocal list.

FCC chair Brendan Carr said 82% of electronic devices authorized for sale in the US in 2025 were tested in China, with under 4% tested in US labs. The rule is drawn by lab geography, not ownership: about 27 labs in China belonging to Intertek, SGS, TÜV Rheinland and Bureau Veritas would be affected.

Of the 609 FCC-recognized test labs, mainland China accounts for 25.1%, Taiwan 18.4% and the US 17.9%. The draft lists more than 60 'reciprocal economies' including Taiwan, Hong Kong, Japan, South Korea, Vietnam and Singapore; mainland China and India are excluded.

The FCC estimates the industry faces about $23.6 million in one-time conversion costs and roughly $79.3 million in added annual testing expenses — FCC certification tests cost $400 to $1,300 in China versus $3,000 to $4,000 in the US — while about 35% of the $57.6 million in annual fees paid to non-reciprocal labs would flow back to US labs.

China has already retaliated: on August 5 its commerce ministry added US-based Compliance Testing LLC to its countermeasure list, and barred US certification bodies from CCC factory inspections. Listed Chinese lab operator CTI said the two-year transition will hit domestic labs but the business is a small share of its revenue.

title: Allwinner Showcases Industrial Chip Lineup at CIIF 2026
body: Allwinner Technology presented its full industrial chip portfolio at the 26th China International Industry Fair, which opened October 12 at Shanghai's National Exhibition and Convention Center, covering six scenarios: PLC, HMI, gateways, power and energy, robotics and industrial vision. Its T153 chip won the fair's 'Guoxin Innovation Achievement Award.'

Four core chips anchor the lineup. The T153 combines a quad-core Arm Cortex-A7 with a single-core RISC-V XuanTie E907, supports DDR3/DDR3L/DDR4, three Gigabit Ethernet ports, two CAN-FD channels and 24-channel GPADC, and targets small and medium PLCs. The T536 pairs a quad-core Cortex-A55 with a 3 TOPS NPU, adds four CAN-FD, 17 UARTs, PCIe and dual Gigabit Ethernet with full-link ECC, aimed at power, energy and industrial control.

The T736 combines dual Cortex-A76 and hexa-core Cortex-A55 CPUs with a PowerVR GPU and 3–4 TOPS NPU, PCIe 3.0, 8K decoding and 4K encoding for edge AI and robotics. The V883 uses a quad-core RISC-V CPU with a 4 TOPS NPU, 4K@75fps encoding, 4K@60fps decoding and up to eight sensor inputs for industrial vision.

More than 14 ecosystem partners exhibited alongside Allwinner, with over 50 industrial boards on display. The company also said it has built a CRA compliance and security service system following IEC 62443-4-1 in development and ISO/IEC 30111 and 29147 for vulnerability response.

title: CanSemi Lists on ChiNext as Guangdong's First 12-Inch Fab, Shares Jump 275% on Debut
body: CanSemi, Guangzhou's 12-inch specialty foundry, debuted on Shenzhen's ChiNext board on October 13, with shares opening 275% above the 12.01-yuan issue price at 45.00 yuan, valuing the company at 129.5 billion yuan.

The listing makes it the first 12-inch wafer manufacturer developed and brought to mass production in Guangdong province, where it has helped the region break from zero in 12-inch wafer manufacturing.
The company plans to use the 7.5 billion yuan raised on a third 12-inch production phase focused on analog specialty processes, plus research projects for specialty process platforms.
CanSemi focuses on analog and mixed-signal nodes from 180nm down to 55nm, reported 2025 revenue of 2.58 billion yuan, and ran its fabs at 96.38% utilization last year.

Planned capacity totals 80,000 wafers per month across its two existing fabs, with a third fab of 40,000 wafers per month under construction, which would bring the combined total to 120,000 wafers per month.

title: Microsoft Unveils Azure Maia 300, Its Third-Generation In-House AI Chip on TSMC 2nm
body: Microsoft has unveiled Azure Maia 300, its third-generation in-house AI inference chip, with the compute chiplet built on TSMC's 2nm process.
Each accelerator pairs eight HBM4 stacks for 288GB of memory and 18TB/s peak bandwidth, delivering 13.8 PFLOPS of FP4 compute at 950W TDP.
Compared with Maia 200, memory bandwidth is 2.5 times higher, capacity is up 33%, and rack-level token throughput reaches up to 7 times higher.

A full rack holds 96 accelerators at 167kW, providing 27.6TB of HBM and 1.7PB/s of aggregate memory bandwidth, and racks scale into a Superpod of up to 12,288 accelerators over a unified electrical-and-optical network.

CEO Satya Nadella called it the company's biggest bet on in-house silicon to date, saying Maia will expand to gigawatt-scale deployments starting next year as the primary inference system for its own products and services.

title: Nanya Posts Record Q3 as DRAM Prices Surge Over 60%, Net Profit Jumps 5,474%
body: Nanya Technology reported record third-quarter results as DRAM average selling prices surged more than 60% quarter on quarter.
Revenue reached NT$133.6 billion, up 611.7% year on year, with gross margin at a record 85.7% and net profit of NT$87.6 billion — a 5,474% year-on-year jump and earnings per share of NT$25.40.

General manager Pei-Ying Lee said AI-driven demand has displaced conventional memory supply, forcing some customers to downgrade specs or even use recycled DRAM, and expects prices to keep rising in the fourth quarter with further gross-margin upside.
AI-infrastructure applications now contribute over 20% of revenue, and AI-ASIC memory projects with Western customers have begun small-volume shipments.

The company also confirmed its 5A fab will begin equipment move-in in the first quarter of 2027, the largest single DRAM investment in Taiwan in nearly two decades at up to NT$346.6 billion (about US$10.7 billion).

title: Four Chinese SiC Startups Close Fresh Funding Rounds
body: Four Chinese silicon-carbide startups have disclosed new funding rounds, underscoring continued capital flowing into the domestic power-semiconductor supply chain.

Xindongneng Semiconductor, incubated by Macro Micro Technology, closed an over-100-million-yuan Series A to expand capacity and R&D for SiC and GaN plastic-packaged power modules, which have already shipped more than 3.8 million units for automotive main-drive inverters.

Xixinwei, an advanced-packaging specialist covering IGBT, SiC and RF, completed a several-hundred-million-yuan Series B and is ramping a new Chengdu base targeting 60,000 wafers per month of packaging output across 6- to 12-inch substrates.

Fermi Electric has accumulated 170 million yuan in funding and says it has built a vertically integrated chain from GaN/SiC chips to power modules and complete systems for solar-storage and marine power applications.
Xinfufa, founded in April 2026, is raising an 8-million-yuan angel round to tape out 3.3kV and 6.5kV SiC devices targeting rail traction and automotive applications.

title: Xinai Technology Raises Over 1 Billion Yuan, Breaks Ground on Second IC-Substrate Fab
body: Nanjing-based IC-substrate maker Xinai Technology announced over 1 billion yuan in strategic financing and broke ground on its second advanced-packaging-substrate fab during a two-day strategy event on October 12–13.

The 1-billion-yuan P2 project will run a fully automated line based on semi-additive (SAP) processes for high-end FCBGA substrates, with 9 million units of annual capacity targeting CPUs, GPUs, ASICs, FPGAs and AI accelerators, and is scheduled to come online in May 2027.
Land for the P3 fab has been secured with construction planned for 2027 and volume production in 2028, maintaining what the company calls a 'one new fab per year' expansion pace.

The new round is Xinai's third major equity financing, bringing cumulative funding to over 3 billion yuan, earmarked for AI and chiplet-architecture substrate capacity, advanced-process iteration and key-customer delivery.
The company says its capacity is concentrated on substrates for 6nm, 4nm and 3nm chips, with products for 2nm nodes expected to enter mass production during 2026.

title: China's Domestic RF Power Supplies Enter Volume-Production Phase
body: China's domestically produced RF power supplies are moving from single-point technology breakthroughs into volume deployment at fabs, entering what the industry calls a scale-up phase for localization of this core semiconductor-equipment component.

The numbers frame the opportunity and the gap: mainland China's semiconductor RF power market was about RMB 6.56 billion in 2024 with domestic vendors holding less than 12%, while globally MKS and Advanced Energy together control roughly 45%-50% of the market — and over 70% inside China.

Hengyunchang (恒运昌) ranked first among domestic vendors in 2024: its Bestda series stably supports 28nm production lines, its Aspen series is in tool qualification for 7-14nm processes, and its products have been adopted by NAURA, AMEC and Tuojing, with qualification completed at SMIC. Injet Electric's (英杰电气) RHH and RPJ series have entered AMEC's and Tuojing's supply chains and are running at a leading memory fab.

Growth is coming from two tracks: matching newly shipped tools and in-situ replacement on existing lines, with SMIC piloting maintenance-swap programs. Qualification cycles have compressed from over six months to a few months, and domestic vendors compete on 24-48-hour on-site service and fast customization.

title: Huawei's Kirin 9050 Pro Brings 'Logic Folding' to Mass Production
body: Huawei held its first offline Kirin-focused media technology briefing in six years on October 13 at its Shanghai Lianqiu Lake campus, where Xu Songyu, head of Huawei's semiconductor wireless terminal chip product management, detailed the Kirin 9050 Pro — the first mass-produced chip built on Huawei's "logic folding" technology, a program the company started exploring four years ago. The chip also made its first offline public appearance at Huawei's terminal innovation tech event on October 12.

Logic folding is not simple die stacking, Huawei says: the chip is designed from the start with a 3D perspective, distributing logic circuits across multiple co-designed DIEs treated as a single chip, which shortens signal routing, raises transistor density, and improves performance and power efficiency.

The Kirin 9050 series packs over 50 million hybrid bonds and more than 5 million effective signal interconnects, lifting transistor density by 53.5%. For the 9050 Pro specifically, Huawei claims a 12.7% higher CPU clock, 41% better big-core CPU efficiency, 40% higher GPU performance, 45% better GPU efficiency, 140% more NPU compute, and 66% better NPU efficiency.

Hybrid bonding is the key enabler: with a 720nm top-metal pitch, the bond pitch must stay under 2µm (pitch ratio below 3); Huawei says it has reached 1.5µm and targets 1µm in 2027, with tighter pitches unlocking more high-speed channels and deeper folding.

Since Kirin's return to the consumer market in 2023, Huawei devices carrying Kirin chips have shipped over 100 million units, the company said. Xu framed the milestone as validation of "time scaling" as a sustainable path forward: "Even though we have temporarily lost geometry-scaling capability, we can still embark on a new 10-year journey."

title: China's Chip Metrology Market Tops RMB 48 Billion as Local Players Chase Sub-15% Share
body: Mainland China's semiconductor metrology and inspection equipment market has surpassed RMB 48 billion and is growing at a compound rate above 17.5%, yet domestic vendors hold less than 15% — and under 5% in the ultra-high-end segment — leaving what the industry calls one of the deepest localization gaps in the chip supply chain.

Global concentration remains extreme: in 2025 KLA held about 53% of the inspection-systems market, followed by Applied Materials (~15%), ASML (~11%), Hitachi High-Tech (~7.8%) and Tokyo Electron (~5%), with the top five taking 91.8% combined; KLA alone holds close to 60% of the China market. Electron-beam inspection is a roughly US$3.3 billion global market, while advanced-packaging inspection and metrology is about US$925 million.

Suzhou-based startup Precise (普雷赛斯) just closed a Series A round on the order of RMB 100 million backed by investors including E-Town Capital, betting on fully in-house development — its core modules exceed 95% self-developed, spanning optical sensing to AI agents — and focusing on advanced-node and advanced-packaging inspection for TSV, RDL, Bump and HBM processes.

title: Chinese SiC Makers Push Toward 12- and 14-Inch Wafers
body: Four Chinese players have disclosed parallel breakthroughs on oversized silicon carbide, pushing from today's 8-inch ramp straight toward 12- and 14-inch formats: a 12-inch wafer yields about 4.4 times as many chips as a 6-inch one, making size the industry's next cost lever.

Hantian Tiancheng (瀚天天成) reported 12-inch (300mm) n-type 4H-SiC epitaxy with thickness non-uniformity improved from 7.68% to 1.72% and doping non-uniformity from 14.62% to 2.15%, reaching 8-inch-equivalent quality and securing small-batch orders. Shanxi Tiancheng (山西天成) demonstrated a 14-inch SiC single crystal with 30mm effective thickness, 90% localized equipment parts, 60 homegrown growth furnaces in phase one, and a phase-two target of 2028 with about RMB 800 million in annual output.

Lijing Xinke (立晶芯科) has developed an AI-assisted 12-inch crystal-growth system — after its first 8-inch PVT ingot in January 2025 and first liquid-phase ingot in June — and expects a high-quality 12-inch single crystal within two months, with pilot samples next year and mass production the year after. A Zhejiang University team separately produced a ~360mm (about 14-inch) polycrystalline SiC ingot by PVT, reporting room-temperature thermal conductivity of about 323.8 W/(m·K).

title: Lithography Startup Milai Xincheng Raises RMB 361 Million
body: Shanghai-based Milai Xincheng Semiconductor (米莱芯程), a projection-exposure (lithography) equipment maker founded in Pudong in March 2025, is raising RMB 361 million in new capital at a RMB 1.5 billion pre-money valuation, with listed investor United Chemical (联合化学) contributing RMB 60 million.

After the round, United Chemical's stake will be diluted from 37.28% to 33.27%. It is the company's third backing from United Chemical, following RMB 120 million in July 2025 (RMB 500 million valuation) and RMB 200 million in November 2025 (RMB 700 million valuation).

Founder and CTO Gao An previously worked at ASML on DUV and EUV projection lithography. The company posted 2025 revenue of RMB 40.48 million with a net loss of RMB 71.84 million, and first-half 2026 revenue of RMB 8.01 million with a RMB 61.59 million loss.

title: Auto Industry Faces Cost 'High Wall' as Memory Prices Spike Post-Holiday
body: China's auto supply chain is facing across-the-board cost hikes after the Golden Week holiday: more than 60 tire makers issued over 70 price-increase letters since September (2%-5%), carbon black prices rose about 45% within a single month, and rubber futures hit a nine-year high.

Memory chips are automakers' biggest pain point: TrendForce reports global conventional DRAM contract prices rose 90%-95% quarter-on-quarter in Q1 2026, while automotive-grade storage purchase prices jumped about 180% between March and June as AI demand crowds out automotive memory capacity.

UBS estimates memory inflation alone adds RMB 3,000-7,000 to the cost of a high-end ADAS vehicle; NIO said its per-vehicle cost rose roughly RMB 14,000 in Q2 versus end-2025, with memory accounting for about RMB 10,000 of that.

Automakers are fighting back with long-term agreements (GM and Ford both signed LTAs with Micron in July), multi-source battery strategies, and material substitution such as aluminum-for-copper; industry profit still fell 16% year-on-year in January-August with a sales margin of just 3.6%.
The article notes China's automotive chip localization rate topped roughly 35% in the first half of 2026, but high-end compute SoCs and high-safety MCUs remain under 5% localized.

title: Domestic Brands Take Over 60% of China's Servo Market as Industrial 'Chip' Momentum Builds
body: China's 2025 general servo market reached RMB 22.96 billion, with domestic brands topping 60% share for the first time (versus under 50% five years ago), while Japanese brands fell from over 50% before 2020 to about 26%, according to GeWu Zhisheng's market white paper.
Low-voltage inverters tell a similar story: the 2025 market was about RMB 29.27 billion, with local brands climbing to 46% and breaking the long-standing ABB/Siemens dominance.

Invosun (汇川技术) holds roughly 22% servo share as the domestic No.1, ahead of Panasonic and Yaskawa, while StarPower Semiconductor earned Invosun's 'strategic supplier' honor in January 2026 with custom-developed IGBT and SiC modules.

Local power-device makers are evolving from build-to-spec suppliers into co-definition partners: Silan Micro is advancing an 'MCU + power module + driver IC' integrated portfolio, and MacroMicro is building a 'chip + module' platform across new energy, EVs, and data centers.

Caveats remain: high-end IGBT modules, precision SiC devices, and high-end IPM modules still lag by a generation and depend heavily on imports, while wide-bandgap cost barriers are slowing large-scale penetration.

title: CW Lasers Emerge as the Tightest Link in the CPO Supply Chain
body: As CPO architecture moves the light source out of the module, a single ultra-high-power CW laser must deliver 400mW of output fiber power and hold it at 55°C or higher; per Coherent's ECOC 2026 architecture, one external light source (ELS) packs up to 8 UHP CW lasers, each split across roughly four links.

Only Lumentum and Coherent publicly supply 400mW-class devices: Nvidia invested $2 billion in each in March 2026 with multi-year purchase commitments, and Coherent said indium phosphide remains its main internal constraint even as June-quarter InP laser output rose about 80% year-on-year.

Domestic vendors are 'delivered at the low end, qualifying at the high end': Yuanjie ships 70mW and 100mW CW lasers in volume (first-half revenue of RMB 925 million, up 351.4% year-on-year, with net profit up 1,212.2%), while its 120mW/300mW/400mW chips are still in qualification; Shijia Photonics ships non-cooled 100mW CW DFB in volume and room-temperature 400mW CW DFB in small volume.

Sanan Optoelectronics plans 400mW sampling for 3.2T optical switches in Q4 2026 with volume shipments in Q1 2027; Accelink and Hisense's Nazhen have high-power models in customer qualification, and Accelink is investing about RMB 6.75 billion toward 800G/1.6T/3.2T capacity.
The article concludes that the real race is not lighting up 400mW in the lab, but ramping yield and capacity at the same time once qualification clears.

title: Domestic Five-Phase Stepper Motors Challenge Long-Standing Japanese Dominance
body: China's 2025 stepper market exceeded RMB 3.2 billion, with industrial steppers at about RMB 2 billion (up 5% year-on-year), per MIR; five-phase steppers — prized for smaller step angles and smoother motion — were long dominated by Japan's Oriental Motor PK/PKP series.

Founded in 2015, Ruite Technology launched a 20mm-flange five-phase motor in 2026 with a 0.72° step angle, filling the hard-to-develop small-frame gap and now covering 20/28/42/60mm — one of the most complete domestic lineups.
Side-by-side repeat-positioning tests of Ruite's 28CM005-D V3.0 against a leading Japanese product on the same drive and platform showed comparable precision.

Ruite's high-performance five-phase solutions are already in volume use on 400G, 800G, and 1.6T optical-module coupling machines, achieving ±0.05μm repeat positioning on XYZ axes in 12-axis FA coupling systems.
The article frames this as domestic steppers moving from single-model replacement toward full product-line coverage of the precision segment.

title: Skyworks Closes $22 Billion Qorvo Merger, Creating RF Powerhouse
body: Skyworks Solutions has completed its previously announced combination with Qorvo, a cash-and-stock transaction valued at approximately $22 billion when it was first announced in October 2025; the deal closed on October 5, 2026 after clearing all regulatory approvals.

Under the terms, Qorvo shareholders received $32.50 in cash plus 0.960 of a Skyworks share for each Qorvo share, leaving legacy Skyworks holders with roughly 63% of the combined company and former Qorvo holders with about 37% on a fully diluted basis.

The combined business keeps the Skyworks name and the SWKS ticker on Nasdaq, and brings together around 8,000 engineers and more than 12,000 issued and pending patents, adding RF GaN, low-voltage power and wired broadband to the portfolio.
Skyworks said the merger more than doubles its addressable market, extending beyond smartphones into defense and aerospace, data center and networking, automotive, edge IoT and AI infrastructure.

The company expects at least $500 million in annualized cost synergies within 24 to 36 months and said the transaction is immediately accretive to non-GAAP earnings per share; part of the cash consideration was financed with $2 billion in senior notes issued in August 2026.

title: Mature-Node Foundry Prices Climb Again in 2026 as 8-Inch Capacity Shrinks
body: Price-hike signals in 2026 have spread from advanced compute and memory into 8-inch foundry services, select 12-inch mature processes, and power devices, with eefocus describing the repricing as structural rather than a repeat of the 2021 shortage.

The timeline: SMIC notified customers late last year of an ~10% increase on 8-inch BCD platforms; TrendForce's January survey found some fabs planning 5%-20% increases; and Chinese power-device vendors including CR Micro, Yangjie, Silan, NCE and MacroMicro announced February adjustments covering MOSFETs, IGBTs and related products.

Through mid-year, Infineon moved customers to new prices effective April 1, STMicroelectronics raised prices in March and again from June 28, and TrendForce's end-June survey showed ~5%-15% average increases on 8-inch foundry across the first half, with 5%-10% increases emerging on tight 12-inch mature nodes in Q2-Q3.

On the capacity side, TrendForce projects TSMC and Samsung will shrink 8-inch capacity faster than additions from SMIC and Vanguard can offset, leaving global 8-inch capacity down ~2.4% year-on-year in 2026.

A key driver is AI: AI server power chains are lifting demand for power management, gate drivers, MOSFETs, DrMOS and smart power stages — demand that runs on mature platforms rather than leading-edge logic.

title: Empyrean's Liu Weiping: Domestic EDA Crosses 'Usable' Threshold, Agentic AI May Reshape the Industry
body: Speaking at CIIF 2026's dedicated IC exhibition in Shanghai on October 12, Empyrean Technology chairman Liu Weiping said commercially deployable domestic EDA tools now cover about 85% of design needs, with nearly 10% at world-leading levels; process-node ecosystem coverage stands near 50% and is targeted at 80% this year.
Empyrean serves nearly 800 customers globally, including seven or eight of the world's top ten chip designers, with more than 6,000 chips designed using its tools.

Liu set three next-phase tasks for China's EDA: supporting indigenous advanced processes, adapting to new 'folded' circuit design methodologies that foreign tools will not support, and rebuilding tool efficiency with AI — where agentic EDA, he said, could change the shape of the entire industry.

title: Hua Hong's Bai Peng: US$1 Trillion Chip Market Arrives a Year Early; Mature Specialty Nodes 'Must Not Be Ignored'
body: At CIIF 2026 in Shanghai, Hua Hong Semiconductor chairman and president Bai Peng said the global IC market will cross US$1 trillion in 2026 — a year earlier than the previously forecast 2027 — driven by AI compute infrastructure and a memory rebound.

The mature-process (22nm and above) foundry market is expected to exceed US$60 billion in 2026, about 27% of global foundry, he said, with mature nodes growing around 6.8% annually — still a stable-growth market, not a shrinking one.

China's foundry capacity now accounts for one-third of the global total, expanding at over 10% CAGR versus 4-5% worldwide; Hua Hong aims to lift its specialty-process ASP ratio from 66% in 2024 to 76% by 2030, targeting 30%, 50%, 20%, 40% and 35% global foundry shares in eFlash, SPI NOR, BCD, CIS and discrete devices respectively by 2030.

title: Xianyi Micro Closes Series A to Scale Magnetic-Isolation Chips, Sets Up East China HQ in Wuxi
body: Shenzhen-based Xianyi Microelectronics, which says it is China's first commercial magnetic-isolation chip company, has closed a Series A round worth tens of millions of yuan led by Xizhou International, and established its East China headquarters in Binhu, Wuxi.

The company says it built China's first commercial magnetic-isolation process line and now offers nearly 300 magnetic-isolation products across signal, interface, driver and power lines, with automotive products AEC-Q100 qualified and in volume supply for industrial and energy-storage applications.

The Wuxi base will serve as its East China R&D and support center, tapping the Yangtze River Delta customer cluster as demand grows in AI compute power infrastructure, solid-state transformers and embodied intelligence — areas where high-voltage isolation requirements are intensifying.

title: Four SiC Projects in China Accelerate Toward Production
